# MovieCellar build log

MovieCellar is a movie collection app for the web and iOS, with a desktop sync agent. An Android build runs in every release gate but is not released. The product is in private beta. AI coding agents (Claude Code and Codex) write the code. I decide what to build, write the specs, and get the agents to build the checks that decide what ships.

This page shows the work as it goes. A script reads the private repository every hour and rewrites this page from counts, dates and a few fixed labels.

**Last change:** 2026-10-05

## Now

- **Commits:** 2,460 on all branches. 2,119 are released. 341 are on branches that are not released yet.
- **Agent share:** 1,891 commits (77%) carry a Claude co-author line. Codex commits and merges carry no such line.
- **Code:** 408,582 lines in 1,959 files. 37% is tests and checks.
- **Size:** 190 route handlers, 90 data models, 466 test files, 17 CI jobs, 11 lint rules.
- **Sprints:** 128 sprint numbers allocated.
- **Release gate:** 109 runs since 2026-09-15. 12 ended ready to ship and 89 ended blocked.
- **Worktrees:** 137 checkouts of the repository, stale ones included. Agents work side by side in separate checkouts.
- **Last release:** 2026-10-05, going by the newest commit on the released branch.
- **Latest commit:** 2026-10-05.

## How this page is made

1. A script reads the private repository. It reads the commit history, the sprint registry and the result files of the release gate, and it counts files and lines.
2. It keeps counts, dates and short commit ids. Gate steps appear under a few fixed labels. A sprint title appears only after it has been approved once.
3. It leaves out code, file names, test names, reviewer notes, clock times and security findings.
4. A scan checks the output for paths, addresses, ids and keys. If it finds one, nothing is published.
5. Nobody reviews an update before it goes out. That is why the script publishes so little.

The same numbers are in the `data` folder as JSON and CSV.
